lessons.introText: Vowels (a, e, i, o, u) have two main sounds. Short vowels are quick and clipped: a as in cat, e as in pen, i as in sit, o as in pot, u as in sun. Long vowels say their own name: a as in cake, e as in bee, i as in bike, o as in cone, u as in cube. A silent e at the end (like cake, bike, cone) usually makes the vowel long. In closed syllables (like cat, sit), the vowel stays short. Listen and compare the pairs below.

sentenceWrite.prompt: Write 2 sentences using the words above.

lessons.introText: Consonants are the other letters of the alphabet. Each makes a distinct sound that shapes words. Listen to the first sound in each word below — that's the consonant sound.

lessons.introText: Short a says /a/ like in apple — when a single vowel is boxed in between two consonants, it usually keeps this quick, clipped sound instead of saying its name. Say each picture word out loud and listen for this pattern.

lessons.introText: Y can make the short vowel /i/ sound. At the end of a one-syllable word, y often borrows the long i sound, turning words like cry and sky into rhymes for 'eye'. Say each picture word out loud and listen for this pattern.

lessons.mainTitle: SHORT WORDS WITH LONG VOWEL SOUNDS
lessons.introText: In some very short, common words, a single e can say its long name, /ee/, all on its own, as in me and he. Say each picture word out loud and listen for this pattern.
